narrative.overview:
SecureMesh uses the Material 3 direction pinned by the product brief. The interface is quiet, task focused and explicit about local persistence, connection state and key comparison. Native controls and readable labels carry the design; the green seed supplies continuity across light and dark themes.

This document records the implemented local alpha and its account-access extension. Current native sources include native.dart, onboarding.dart and account_hub.dart with the shared HTTP, local-client, session and delivery/transport code. Reusable account forms keep the account password separate from the local encrypted-store passphrase. The account hub separates chat consent, unchecked explicit key comparison and device enrollment. Pending, server-approved, locally verified and activated states remain distinct; local verification is an intermediate operation, not a separate success screen. Approval never implies old-history transfer or recovery, which remain unavailable. A conclusive unauthenticated rejection releases the prepared form identity for correction while retaining the unused encrypted file; action errors persist across successful background refreshes.

The extension preserves the incumbent token frontmatter and preview CSS. Frontmatter uses portable CSS units corresponding to Flutter logical pixels and unscaled type sizes; message width is a maximum. Actual Linux GTK/Xvfb review captures include 1280×720 desktop and 320×844 compact registration, login, comparison, conversation and offline/recovered states. phone.png is a compact Linux window, not a mobile build. Screenshots are test evidence, not shipping raster assets. Retained analyzer, widget, Linux-build, GUI and enrollment process logs were inspected, not rerun by the documenter. New account dark flows, mobile platforms, full native enrollment, assistive technology and independent security assurance remain unverified. Product status is PARTIAL / NOT_READY; four reported RustSec findings remain and PRODUCTION_APPROVED=false.
keyCharacteristics: Material controls with one green seed and semantic light/dark roles.
Reusable account forms that distinguish server credentials from the local encrypted-store passphrase.
Explicit contact comparison and staged device approval before account use.
Separate connection, queue and message-persistence labels.
Compact bottom navigation and expanded navigation rail.
Russian/English application labels and selectable message/key text.
Visible local-alpha limitations without readiness or audit claims.

rules.name: The Theme Role Rule
rules.body: Keep the generated light/dark role relationship. The frontmatter captures this dependency version; `ColorScheme.fromSeed` remains the implementation source of truth.

dos: Do use Material 3 controls and current theme roles for new native UI.
Do keep persistence, connection and key confirmation explicit in text.
Do distinguish account credentials, local-store ownership, server approval, local verification and device activation.
Do preserve readable action errors across background refreshes and give a deliberate retry path.
Do retain RU/EN strings, selectable message/key text and labeled actions.
Do validate compact/expanded, light/dark and large-text behavior after UI changes.
Do preserve the local-alpha scope notice until implementation and evidence change.
donts: Don't hardcode the light palette into dark-mode widgets.
Don't imply read or peer-delivered receipts from server acknowledgement.
Don't imply that an account password or device approval transfers old history or provides recovery.
Don't substitute visual polish for device-trust, offline-queue or accessibility verification.
Don't claim completed groups, media, calls, browser private chat, mobile verification or independent audit.
Don't treat the sidecar's HTML previews as production Flutter widgets or platform test evidence.
